title: Desk cable organiser with five clips
prompt: Desk cable organiser for five USB cables (5 mm thick). A 90 x 20 x 3 mm base strip with two M4 clearance holes (4.5 mm) on its centre line, 5 mm in from each end, and five snap-in clips standing on top, 15 mm apart and centred along the strip. Each clip is 10 mm long along the cable (centred on the strip's width) and is a C-shaped ring: 5.2 mm inside diameter, 1.5 mm wall, its centre 3.5 mm above the top of the base so the bottom of the ring sits flat on the base, with a 3.6 mm opening at the top to push the cable in; cut the opening with radial faces. Base centred on the origin, sitting on Z = 0, long side along X, so the cables run along Y.

hidden_tests.description: Evaluates cleanly and every body is a valid closed solid
Six solids: the base and five clips
90 x 20 mm footprint, 9.46 mm tall (3 + 3.5 + the top of the radial lips)
Base centred on the origin, on Z = 0
Five clips: 8.2 mm wide rings (1.5 mm wall), 10 mm long, standing on the base top (Z = 3)
Five 5.2 mm cable seats (5.1–5.3: a snug fit on 5 mm cables)
15 mm pitch: a clip centred at X = 15 …
… and an end clip at X = −30 (five clips centred on the strip)
Two M4 clearance holes (4.4–4.6 mm) on the centre line, 5 mm from each end

notes: Clip profile area (closed form): outer disc above the base line [πR² − (R²·acos(3.5/R) − 3.5·√(R² − 3.5²))] − bore πr² − opening wedge ½(π − 2θ)(R² − r²), R = 4.1, r = 2.6, θ = atan2(√(r² − 1.8²), 1.8) = 22.153 mm². The 3.6 mm opening is narrower than the 5 mm cable: it snaps in.
